descriptionHtml:
Bug B18 · P1 · known

Many dates and times follow the device clock instead of server time (UAT 3.8): 'NEW TODAY', admit date, vitals date, task done time, transcript date; with a phone two days slow a held drug is stamped two days back and the next cleanup deletes it

Tickets: TFA-92584 ready for qa (UAT 3.8); TFA-92597 ready for qa (R6); TFA-92579 AC 3/4 ready for qa (NEW TODAY); TFA-94745 ready for qa (draft restore) · counts as a QA bug: yes · found on: local

Note: Root cause known (Daniela asked for server time on 10-03); the deleted drug, missing badge and wrong draft restore are new symptoms. TC-16/S18 (UAT 3.8, one device set to the wrong date): a phone a day ahead files its bedside line in a row dated tomorrow on the shared record, and the next write from a correctly clocked device lists the lines before it twice (the transcript archive trusts the device date). Which calendar day a correct device should use when its local day and the server's UTC day differ is the open question Q9 (D10); TC-16/S25 passed otherwise. Review 2026-10-14 (TFA-92579/92584): a browser whose day is ahead writes the badge roll back to the server, and every device shows Follow-up, with the matching template and billing family (TC-01/S08, TC-20/S20a; TFA-92584 AC 8). The failing cell of TC-25/S24a is the card's NEW TODAY, which compares addedAt with the device's date (PatientCard.tsx:154-156). EFS/S28 (a)(b) restore drafts by the device date (TFA-94745); (c), an old draft put in today's box, is B13's. Review 2026-10-15 (TFA-94514): the analytics day is the device date too (pilotUsageEvents / pilotDailyRounding use localDay()): a phone 3 days ahead files its rows under its own day, and an encounter across the phone midnight is split over two days and never timed (OAT-06/S10). Re-test 2026-10-16 (TC-21/S26, 25acd727): a browser two days ahead writes the badge roll with its own future day (encTypeDay 2026-10-19) to the shared record, so the correct-clock browser shows Follow-up too.

Other cases of the same bug (counted once): TC-01/S08, TC-10/S22, TC-12/S23, TC-19/S19, TC-22/S23, TC-25/S24a, TC-02/S13b, EFS/S28, TC-16/S18, TC-06/S19, OAT-06/S10, TC-06/S23, TC-21/S22, TC-25/S24b, TC-19/S23

Approach · TC-21 Hospital vs. Nursing-Home Context Switch · S26 Server clock, not device clock: two browser contexts, one 2 days ahead in another time zone, show the same state

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • G3.8 Every time-based rule uses the server clock: retention, carry-forward, the day roll to Follow-up, 'today' on the timeline and the hospital day / visit number. … (UAT 3.8; TFA-92584 AC 8) — gate: blocked: TFA-92599 in progress
  • U1a Visit cadence changes per context. Hospital shows the hospital day, which advances each server calendar day and never freezes. … (UAT TC-21 step 1; UAT TC-01; UAT TC-11) — gate: blocked: TFA-92599 in progress
  • U4 Default template: the admission-status badge pre-selects the template (New Admission → H&P / SNF admission, Follow-up → SOAP progress / SNF follow-up, Consult → Consult note / SNF consult), and the p … (UAT TC-21; UAT TC-21 step 1 (default template); TFA-92599 AC 6; TFA-92599 rule 4; TFA-92584 AC 6) — gate: blocked: TFA-92599 in progress

Test design technique: Boundary values (boundary) — Sit right on the edge of the rule (exactly on time / a minute late, empty, longest, most) and see on which side the behavior changes.

Given The same @roundai.test account in two Playwright browser contexts on the local stack. Context B uses page.clock.setSystemTime(now + 2 days) and timezoneId 'Pacific/Kiritimati' (UTC+14). Hospital patient and resident badges set to New Admission today in context A.

When In Hospital and in Nursing Home, open the list, the chart's Encounter tab and the course timeline in both contexts

Then The card's day / visit number, the badge (no day roll on B only), the badge-preselected Note Format option and the timeline's 'today' line are identical in A and B

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): Equality between A and B per item (3.8). Today the existing lane A spec decides only the timeline's 'today' line; the rest needs the runnerGap spec. Pre-labelled: the day roll and badge default still use the device clock (known: TFA-92584 AC 8; AppLayout.tsx and useNoteFormats call localDay()). A real phone with a wrong clock is S22.

Where it ran: local newspec-c (new Playwright specs); test method PW · Playwright script; lane planned in the matrix: existing tests (Tim's Playwright) (automated)

S26 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/TC-21.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Triage (2026-10-14): 0 rows.

Environment: local — main e02167f → 25acd727 (10-15/16/17 re-tests), local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane newspec-c.

Test method: PW · Playwright script; secondary: MULTI · Multi-device / multi-account — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on both; Source: newspec-c.

UAT item: TC-21 Hospital vs. Nursing-Home Context Switch · Section: A5 · Cross-Cutting · Scenario: TC-21/S26

Server clock, not device clock: two browser contexts, one 2 days ahead in another time zone, show the same state

Tickets: TFA-92584 Admission Status Toggle (ready for qa); TFA-92599 Hospital vs. Nursing-Home Context Switch (ready for qa)

Re-verdict after the QA review of TFA-92584 (2026-10-14; not yet checked by Quinn): needs a person. Only the course-timeline cell (today's row uses server time, TFA-92589) ran; the card day count, the badge and the Note Format cells did not. TC-01/S08 and TC-20/S20a already show the badge cell fails (TFA-92584 AC 8, B18). The run's own result was product; its evidence is below.

New local lane newspec-c: status failed in newspec-c/results.json → failed · product (failed · product (the lane flagged a product issue; part of it is a known gap)).

Detail:

Local 25acd727, runnerGap R7 spec: same account in two browser contexts; A on the real clock, B with the clock 2 days ahead and time zone Pacific/Kiritimati (UTC+14, signed in again through the form after its session read as expired). Patient and resident set New Admission today. 0/8 judged equal: B shows Follow-up where A shows New Admission (Hospital and NH), so B pre-selects SOAP progress / SNF follow-up where A pre-selects H&P / SNF admission; the list cards differ (A 'NEW TODAY … New Admission', B '… Follow-up'); B's Hospital Course Timeline shows no card for today's line ('Oct 16: …') that A shows. And B's route lifecycle wrote its own day to the shared record: both rows became follow-up@2026-10-19 (a day that has not come yet), so afterwards A also shows Follow-up / SOAP progress / SNF follow-up. Known B18 (TFA-92584 AC 8, UAT 3.8). The lane-A cell (Tim's 'today's line is dated by the server clock, not the device's') passed on 43c38a4f; it stores a note so it is not re-run locally, and the code it covers is unchanged on 25acd727 (git diff 43c38a4f 25acd727 has no change under src/domain, src/features/snf/patient/EncounterTab.tsx or AppLayout.tsx).

Product issue: A device whose clock is ahead shows New Admission patients as Follow-up with the follow-up template pre-selected, and it saves that roll with its own future date, so every other device then shows Follow-up too (known B18).

Known gap (known): true

Evidence: 4 attached.

Dev run: skipped: local-only — local-only — Lane A: a Playwright spec with two browser contexts on fresh @roundai.test accounts (one context with page.clock and timezoneId), made with the local stack's admin key; dev has one shared account and no admin key, so it runs on the local stack only (Quinn 2026-10-14).. This local result replaces that dev entry (the scenario appears once).

This case has results elsewhere too (a case shows one result: a verdict beats blocked, a run beats a skip; within a tier the worse one, on a tie the earlier one (dev, dev lanes, local lane A/C, new local lanes), test out of date ranks above passed; when all are skips the dev one, unless dev only says "local only / can't run on dev" or gives the lane's own reason):

  • [local matrix (lane A)] passed (matrix/TC-21.results.json)
